standard: GDD rework v2 · 80+ researched scenarios · scorecard-passed
note: Fertility, pregnancy & contraception (UNESCO 6.2, 8.1). New v2 build, Chapter 4 (real, matter-of-fact, values-first). GATED (school-comfort). Delaying is fully valid & respected; accurate facts bust dangerous myths; contraception at an age-appropriate overview level. Builds on g14; prereq g39. Non-judgmental, non-explicit; routes to a doctor/trusted adult for facts.
evidenceBase: Pregnancy can happen any time sperm meets egg, including the first time and (less likely) during a period; withdrawal and douching are unreliable, and orgasm is not required, common myths endanger teens

Not having sex is the only fully reliable way to avoid pregnancy and is a completely valid, respected choice; condoms prevent pregnancy and STIs, and several other methods exist that a doctor can explain
High-quality comprehensive sexuality education delays sexual initiation and increases protection use, it does not encourage earlier sex; accurate facts from a doctor or trusted adult beat rumours

scenarios.hook: "You can't get pregnant the first time."

myth.un: You can't get pregnant the first time.
myth.re: Pregnancy is possible the very first time, every time carries a chance.
myth.why: The body doesn't get a 'free pass' on the first occasion.

scenarios.relearn: You can get pregnant the first time; there's no 'free pass'.

scenarios.hook: "You can't get pregnant during your period."

myth.un: It's impossible to get pregnant during a period.
myth.re: It's less likely but still possible, especially with shorter or irregular cycles.
myth.why: Sperm can live for days and cycles vary.

scenarios.relearn: Pregnancy during a period is less likely but still possible.

scenarios.hook: "Pulling out in time prevents pregnancy."

myth.un: Pulling out (withdrawal) reliably prevents pregnancy.
myth.re: Withdrawal is unreliable; fluid before climax can contain sperm.
myth.why: About 1 in 5 who rely on it each year have an unplanned pregnancy.

scenarios.relearn: Withdrawal is unreliable; it isn't a dependable method.

scenarios.hook: "If she doesn't orgasm, she can't get pregnant."

myth.un: Pregnancy needs the girl to orgasm.
myth.re: Orgasm has nothing to do with whether an egg gets fertilised.
myth.why: Fertilisation is about sperm meeting egg, not pleasure.

scenarios.relearn: Orgasm isn't required for pregnancy; that myth is false.

scenarios.hook: "Washing or douching afterwards stops pregnancy."

myth.un: Washing or douching after sex prevents pregnancy.
myth.re: It does not; sperm can already be on the way.
myth.why: You can't rinse away the possibility.

scenarios.relearn: Douching or washing afterwards does not prevent pregnancy.

scenarios.hook: "Standing up or jumping afterwards prevents it."

myth.un: Position, standing or jumping afterwards prevents pregnancy.
myth.re: None of these affect whether sperm reaches an egg.
myth.why: Gravity tricks are myths.

scenarios.relearn: Position and 'tricks' afterwards don't prevent pregnancy.

scenarios.hook: "You're too young for your body to get pregnant."

scenarios.relearn: Once puberty begins, pregnancy is biologically possible.

scenarios.hook: "Only certain 'types' of people need to know this."
